not_modelled.DirectMessageV2 request frame: A BYTE frame — fixed-width length prefixes over raw bytes (message_id 16 bytes, u8 endpoint lengths, u32 payload length), not a JSON document. JSON Schema cannot express it, and pretending otherwise would produce a contract that validates nothing an implementation actually parses. It stays with the codec, and cross-implementation agreement on it belongs in fixtures/direct-v2/ as byte vectors. ADR-0049 records this exact case as a revisit condition: byte-level framing is where Protobuf or CDDL would earn its place.
not_modelled.AcceptedV2 / RejectedV2 responses: Byte frames for the same reason. Their vocabularies ARE modelled — see reject-reason — because the coarse code set is what a reviewer needs to check against the privacy rule, and it is stable independently of how the bytes are laid out.
